**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
Two competing Senate budget resolutions (S.Con.Res. 38, S.Con.Res. 39) sit on the Legislative Calendar with ten-year revenue, debt, and reconciliation instructions that directly bind Treasury's borrowing authority and tax policy agenda. The continuing resolution landscape is active: H.R. 6500 is in Senate-to-House message status and H.R. 9770 has been received in the Senate. Funding gaps at either stage create operational risk for IRS and Fiscal Service.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred at 57 days. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) returned at 228 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (Assistant Secretaries) all withdrawn after extended delays. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains a priority gap.

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
FinCEN published a revised Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting rule (Aug. 14) and issued a Minnesota Geographic Targeting Order (Aug. 11). IRS finalized backup withholding guidance on third-party network transactions (Aug. 10). Two FIO elimination bills (H.R. 643, S. 5158) are active in both chambers.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee holds FinCEN oversight hearing; Director Andrea Gacki testifies.

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 7147 became P.L. 119-86, extending FY2026 continuing appropriations. Funding levels remain below operational baseline, sustaining execution risk for IRS filing-season readiness and debt management. FinCEN's beneficial ownership reporting revision published Aug. 14 and a Minnesota geographic targeting order published Aug. 11 are active implementation priorities.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred, pending 56 days. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) returned after 227 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel), Trennert, and Petit withdrawn after extended holds. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Ways and Means received three bills: H.R. 10090 (excise tax on higher education institutions over athletic participation), H.R. 10060 (mandatory presidential audit), and H.R. 10049 (VITAL Act housing tax credit). H.R. 10044 AI Tax and Work Protection Act referred jointly to Ways and Means. Backup withholding rule on third-party network transactions published Aug. 10.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee scheduled oversight hearing on FinCEN. Director Andrea Gacki is the sole witness. Staff should prepare members on BOI reporting revision and GTO activity.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies today before House Financial Services. The Beneficial Ownership Information reporting revision rule (pub. Aug. 14) will likely draw questions. Treasury should anticipate oversight pressure on BOI implementation timelines and enforcement posture.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
IRS Chief Counsel nominee Gadwood remains in committee (55 days). Kothari (Asst. Secretary) was returned after 226 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (Asst. Secretaries) were all withdrawn. Two IRS Chief Counsel slots have now cycled without confirmation.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Ways and Means activity is heavy. Key bills to track: H.R. 10104 (dyed fuel penalty repeal, Highway Trust Fund revenue risk); H.R. 10060 (presidential audit mandate, IRS independence and resources); H.R. 9801 (ABLE MATCH, Section 529A fiscal exposure); H.R. 10044 (AI tax provisions, novel classification questions). GTO targeting Minnesota financial institutions published Aug. 11. Backup withholding rule on third-party networks published Aug. 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype — not an official product*
**[DATE]**

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies before House Financial Services today. FinCEN's BOI reporting rule published August 14 and a Minnesota geographic targeting order published August 11 will likely draw member questions on compliance scope and small-business burden.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
IRS Chief Counsel nominee Gadwood was referred to the full Senate at day 54. Prior nominees Kothari (Asst. Secretary, 225d) and Korb (IRS Chief Counsel, 271d) were returned or withdrawn. Three additional Asst. Secretary slots remain unfilled after withdrawals.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
H.R. 10104 would eliminate dyed-fuel excise penalties, risking trust fund revenue erosion. H.R. 10090 imposes a new college athletics excise tax with significant IRS implementation burden. H.R. 9801 expands ABLE account matching under IRC 529A. H.R. 7147 is now Public Law 119-86; Treasury should confirm IRS and Fiscal Service funding continuity. Backup withholding rules on third-party network transactions published August 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies today before House Financial Services. The BOI reporting requirement revision published August 14 remains the highest-visibility active rulemaking. H.R. 7147 is now Public Law 119-86, providing continuing appropriations for Treasury operations including IRS.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) was referred to the full Senate at day 53. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) was returned after 224 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (both Assistant Secretary) were withdrawn after 270, 381, and 550 days respectively. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Active bills of note: H.R. 10104 eliminates dyed-fuel penalties, creating excise tax revenue and compliance risk. H.R. 10090 imposes a new IRS-administered excise tax on higher education institutions. H.R. 9801 creates ABLE account matching contributions requiring IRS design and SSA coordination. The BOI revision and Minnesota geographic targeting order require near-term monitoring.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TOP LINE**
H.R. 6500, the FY2027 continuing resolution, passed the Senate and returns to the House. Treasury's Fiscal Service and debt issuance operations remain exposed until enactment. H.R. 8595 and H.R. 9770, both received in the Senate, carry appropriations for TFI/OFAC and core departmental offices including IRS and FinCEN. Funding gaps across any of these vehicles would impair sanctions enforcement, tax administration, and cash management functions.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) was referred to the full Senate at day 52. Four nominations remain stalled or cleared: Kothari returned at day 223; Korb and Trennert withdrawn at days 269 and 380 respectively; Petit withdrawn at day 549. IRS Chief Counsel and two Assistant Secretary slots remain unfilled.

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Senate Finance received S. 5227 (First-Time Homebuyer) and S. 5216 (Senior Accessible Housing Tax Credit); House companions H.R. 7468 and H.R. 9554 also active. S. 3333 (Emergency Savings Enhancement) calendared in the Senate. All engage IRS administration and OTP scoring. FinCEN published a Geographic Targeting Order for Minnesota (Aug. 11). Backup withholding rules on third-party network transactions published Aug. 10.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: FinCEN oversight hearing, witness Director Andrea Gacki.

**TOP LINE**
Five nominations in the IRS Chief Counsel and Treasury Assistant Secretary pipeline remain stalled or cleared: Gadwood referred at 51 days, Kothari returned at 222 days, Korb withdrawn at 268 days, Trennert withdrawn at 379 days, and Petit withdrawn at 548 days. IRS leadership gaps persist. FinCEN Director Gacki testifies before House Financial Services today.

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred, awaiting floor action. Kothari (Asst. Secretary) returned to the White House. Three prior nominees withdrawn after extended delays; no replacements announced.

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
Ways and Means received H.R. 10075 (first-time homebuyer tax credit). Senate Finance received S. 5285 (accessible housing credits) and S. 5350 (energy tax provisions). Foreign Relations received S. 5356 (Lebanon sanctions/OFAC). Monitor H.R. 10014 (appropriations accountability) for Treasury funding implications. FinCEN issued a Geographic Targeting Order for Minnesota financial institutions (Aug. 11). IRS backup withholding rules on third-party network transactions published Aug. 10.

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official Treasury product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
FinCEN Director Gacki testifies before House Financial Services today. Treasury published a Geographic Targeting Order for Minnesota financial institutions Monday, adding to recent FinCEN activity. The nominations pipeline shows five IRS and Treasury Assistant Secretary slots stalled or withdrawn, leaving key leadership gaps.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) was referred to the full Senate 50 days ago, no floor action scheduled. Kothari (Treasury Assistant Secretary) was returned after 221 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel), Trennert, and Petit (both Treasury Assistant Secretary) were withdrawn after prolonged delays.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Finance Committee received nine IRC-amending bills this cycle covering critical minerals extraction tax parity, retirement plan simplification, refund procedures, installment agreement fees, EFIN preparer credentialing, taxpayer advocate authorities, and clinical trial income exclusions. Ways and Means received two bills on homeowners insurance deductions and domestic manufacturing incentives. Treasury published a backup withholding rule on third-party network transactions and finalized corrections to QDOT regulations under Section 2056A.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Andrea Gacki, FinCEN Director.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
Senate passed H.R. 6500 (CR/Extensions, FY2027) 90-6. Fiscal Service continuity risk is resolved near-term pending House concurrence. Senate also cleared H.R. 5366 (disaster tax relief) by UC; IRS faces system and guidance updates. Digital asset cloture (H.R. 3633) was filed, putting BSA/FinCEN reconciliation questions in active play.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred, 49 days pending. Kothari (Asst. Secretary) returned after 220 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert (Asst. Secretary) withdrawn. Petit (Asst. Secretary) withdrawn at 546 days. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
FinCEN published a Geographic Targeting Order for Minnesota financial institutions (Aug. 11). IRS backup withholding rule for third-party network transactions published Aug. 10. S. 5275 (presidential audit mandate) and S. 5322 (scholarship tax credits) referred to Finance.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY LEGISLATIVE AFFAIRS — MORNING HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype. Not an official product.*

---

**TOP LINE**
Senate passed H.R. 6500, the FY2027 continuing appropriations bill, 90-6 with an amendment. OLA and OMB must review the amendment text for riders or funding limitations affecting IRS, FinCEN, OFR, and Departmental Offices. Senate also passed H.R. 5334, the Graham Russia-Iran Sanctions Act, 86-11; OLA should obtain bill text to assess OFAC implementation requirements.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) remains in committee, referred 48 days ago. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) was returned after 219 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert and Petit (both Assistant Secretaries) were withdrawn after 265, 376, and 545 days respectively. IRS Chief Counsel vacancy remains unresolved.

---

**LEGISLATION AND RULES**
Cloture filed on H.R. 3633, Digital Asset Market Clarity Act; TFI and FinCEN should assess AML and OFAC compliance gap risks. S. 1525, Common Cents Act, passed Senate; U.S. Mint must plan penny wind-down. H.R. 5366 disaster tax relief bill passed; IRS guidance required. IRS backup withholding rule on third-party network transactions published August 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype — not an official product*
**[Today's Date]**

---

**TOP LINE**
Senate passed H.R. 6500, the continuing resolution, 90-6. The bill funds Treasury operations including Fiscal Service, debt management, and payment systems pending full-year appropriations. H.R. 5334, the Graham Russia-Iran sanctions act, passed 86-11 and moves to the House. S. 1525, the Common Cents Act eliminating the penny, passed by unanimous consent, implicating the Mint and Bureau of Engraving and Printing. Cloture filed on H.R. 3633, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, raising OFAC and FinCEN jurisdictional concerns.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) referred, day 47. Kothari (Assistant Secretary) returned after 218 days. Korb (IRS Chief Counsel) and Trennert (Assistant Secretary) withdrawn at 264 and 375 days respectively. Petit (Assistant Secretary) withdrawn at 544 days. IRS Chief Counsel slot remains vacant.

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
H.R. 5366, disaster tax relief, passed Senate without amendment, requiring IRS guidance updates. S. 5369, Nicaragua sanctions reauthorization, referred to Foreign Relations, broadening potential OFAC workload. Treasury published a backup withholding rule on third-party network transactions August 10.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.

**TREASURY HILL BRIEF**
*Public-source prototype — not an official product*

---

**TOP LINE**
The Senate passed S. 3977, the Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act, raising Subchapter V debt limits. Treasury should assess fiscal exposure for federally backed lenders. H.R. 5334, the Graham Russia-Iran sanctions bill, moved to the Senate floor; OFAC faces expanded designation and licensing workload. H.R. 8595, the FY2027 national security appropriations bill, was received in the Senate; TFI and FinCEN funding levels are at stake.

---

**NOMINATIONS**
Four nominees are in early referral status: Brooke (Deputy Secretary), Kothari, McMaster (Assistant Secretaries), and Browne (Under Secretary), all referred within two days. Gadwood (IRS Chief Counsel) remains pending at 46 days. Three nominations were withdrawn: Trennert (374 days), Petit (543 days), and Korb (263 days).

---

**LEGISLATION & RULES**
S. 5073 and S. 5072 were referred to Senate Finance, targeting IRS complexity, fraud, and taxpayer notice requirements. S. 1525 (Common Cents Act) implicates U.S. Mint coinage authority. Treasury published a final Title VI regulatory rescission August 3.

---

**HEARINGS**
House Financial Services Subcommittee: Oversight of FinCEN. Witness: Director Andrea Gacki.
